.. _lvgl_gpio:

=========================================
2.3 Switch and Checkbox — RGB LED Control
=========================================

Controlling physical hardware (WS2812 LED) with LVGL switch and checkbox widgets.

Overview
========

This is the first project where GUI widgets interact directly with hardware. You'll use a **Switch** to toggle an LED on/off and **Checkboxes** (radio-button style) to select colors.

What You'll Learn
=================

* Creating and styling switches (``lv_switch``) and checkboxes (``lv_checkbox``)
* Single-selection radio-button behavior
* Linking GUI events to hardware actions (``neopixelWrite()``)
* Dynamic label updates showing device state

How the Code Works
==================

**Master Switch**

.. code-block:: cpp

   static void switch_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
       bool on = lv_obj_has_state(btn, LV_STATE_CHECKED);
       if (on) applyColor(); else neopixelWrite(48, 0, 0, 0);
   }

**Color Selection (Radio-Style)**

Multiple checkboxes are linked so only one can be active at a time. Each maps to an RGB color:

.. code-block:: cpp

   // Red checkbox
   lv_obj_t *cb_red = lv_checkbox_create(lv_scr_act());
   lv_checkbox_set_text(cb_red, "Red");
   // ... style with red indicator ...

   static void cb_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
       selectedColor = RED;
       if (masterSwitchOn) applyColor();
   }

**6 Colors**: Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, Cyan, Magenta

Expected Result
===============

- The master switch toggles the WS2812 LED on/off
- Selecting a color checkbox changes the LED color immediately
- The status label shows the current LED state (ON/OFF and color)

The WS2812 LED on GPIO 48 responds in real-time to the touchscreen controls.
